scandal: Gross flat-financing scandal
note: Prime minister resigned over unexplained financing of his flat; the same coalition continued under Paroubek (date: resignation 25 Apr, accepted 26 Apr)

scandal: Dismissal of anti-corruption chief (KNAB) and protests
note: Kalvitis announced on 7 Nov that he would step down on 5 Dec; the cabinet resigned 5 Dec; a near-identical coalition returned under Godmanis

scandal: Mahon Tribunal inquiry into the Taoiseach's finances
note: Ahern announced on 2 Apr he would resign on 6 May; Cowen succeeded in the same coalition. Ahern said the tribunal did not motivate the decision; most outlets linked them

scandal: Fortis affair: alleged interference with the judiciary
note: Government offered its resignation on 19 Dec, accepted 22 Dec; Van Rompuy (same party, same coalition) took over

scandal: President Wulff: home loan and favours
note: Head of state resigned a day after prosecutors asked parliament to lift his immunity; the government was not affected

scandal: President Schmitt: plagiarised doctoral thesis
note: Head of state resigned after his doctorate was revoked; an academic-integrity scandal, not corruption; the government was not affected

scandal: Anti-corruption commission report on the prime minister's assets
note: Report of 7 Jan 2013; coalition partner left; government lost a constructive no-confidence vote on 27 Feb. The part of the report on Jansa was later annulled by the Supreme Court

scandal: Nagygate: bribery and abuse of the intelligence service by the PM's chief of staff
note: Necas announced on 16 Jun and resigned on 17 Jun; caretaker cabinet and early election in Oct 2013

scandal: SREL intelligence service scandal (illegal surveillance, misuse of funds)
note: Parliamentary inquiry found the PM politically responsible; the Social Democrat partner withdrew; snap election 20 Oct 2013. An abuse-of-power scandal with some corruption allegations

scandal: Ponta on trial for corruption; Colectiv fire protests against corruption
note: Government resigned after street protests triggered by a deadly nightclub fire; the PM had been on trial for corruption since Sep 2015. Mixed trigger: safety failure plus corruption. Technocratic cabinet followed

scandal: Deputy PM and HDZ leader Karamarko: conflict of interest (MOL lobbyist)
note: Karamarko resigned on 15 Jun after the ethics watchdog found a conflict of interest; the government lost a no-confidence vote on 16 Jun; snap election Sep 2016

scandal: Gurtel verdict: People's Party kickbacks-for-contracts scheme
note: Rajoy lost a no-confidence vote on 1 Jun; Sanchez (PSOE) became prime minister without an election

scandal: Murder of journalist Jan Kuciak investigating government-linked corruption
note: Fico announced on 14 Mar, accepted 15 Mar; Pellegrini (same party and coalition) took over. The trigger was the murder and the corruption links it exposed, not a charge against Fico

scandal: Ibiza video: vice-chancellor Strache offering contracts for support
note: Strache resigned and Kurz ended the coalition on 18 May; Kurz lost a no-confidence vote on 27 May; early election Sep 2019

scandal: Murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia and links to the PM's office
note: Muscat announced on 1 Dec that he would resign once a new party leader was chosen, and left office in Jan 2020; Abela (same party) succeeded

scandal: Childcare benefits scandal
note: Cabinet resigned two months before a scheduled election. Institutional wrongdoing by the tax authority, not personal corruption: kept in the main sample, tested without

scandal: Centre Party Porto Franco influence-peddling investigation
note: Ratas resigned and the cabinet fell; a Reform-Centre coalition under Kallas replaced it

scandal: Kurz investigated for corruption and bribery (public funds for favourable coverage)
note: Kurz stepped down on 9 Oct, three days after prosecutors named him a suspect; Schallenberg (same coalition) succeeded

scandal: Lithium and hydrogen corruption probe (Operation Influencer)
note: Costa resigned hours after his chief of staff was detained; parliament dissolved; early election Mar 2024

scandal: President Novak: pardon in a child-abuse cover-up case
note: Head of state and the former justice minister resigned over a controversial pardon; an abuse-of-office scandal; the government was not affected

scandal: Spinumviva: prime minister's family company and conflict of interest
note: The government lost its own confidence motion on 11 Mar after the opposition announced an inquiry; early election May 2025

scandal: Prime minister's business dealings and EU-subsidised purchases
note: Paluckas resigned on 31 Jul under pressure from the president and a coalition partner; a new prime minister from the same party followed
